subject: food-technology
title: Macronutrients in Depth: Application
welcome_lead: Apply UK guidelines — about 50% carbs, 15% protein, 35% fat — to real meals.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE macronutrients: UK percentage intakes, saturated vs unsaturated fats.
final_note: Apply percentages to plates, not just to exam papers.

walkthroughs.body_html: UK guidance suggests roughly 50% of energy from carbohydrate, about 15% from protein and about 35% from fat, with no more than 11% from saturated fat. Use these as targets when planning a day's meals.

Not all fats are equal. Saturated fats (butter, fatty meat) raise LDL cholesterol. Unsaturated fats (olive oil, oily fish, nuts) lower it. Trans fats from hydrogenated oils are the worst — most are now banned or phased out.

Meat, fish, eggs, dairy and soya are complete proteins. Most plant sources are missing one or two essential amino acids — but combining rice with beans, or hummus with bread, supplies the full set across a meal.
